text:
I locked the car door
and when I looked up I saw this guy
walking toward me
he looked like Peter, my old friend
but he wasn’t Peter
he was a gaunt man
in jeans and a blue work shirt
and he said to me:

“hey, my wife and I
need something to eat,
we’re starving”

I looked behind him
and there she was,
his wife
who looked at me with eyes
on the verge of tears.

I gave him a five-dollar bill.

“I love you, man!” he shouted,
“I won’t spend it on booze.”

“Why not?” I answered,
“That’s what I would do…”

I walked away to enter a building
settled a few matters
came out
returned to the car
as always
thinking
whether I had done the right thing
or whether I had been conned.


while driving
I remembered my years
of misery
hungry beyond any remedy
I never asked anyone
for a cent.


that night, after a few drinks,
I explained to the woman I lived with
how much money I gave to bums
but how I
in the darkest times
of hunger in my life
refused to ask anyone for anything.


“the thing is, you weren’t even
good at that,” she said.

translation.title: I Locked the Car Door...
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. Dialogue, lowercase presentation, and lineation are preserved.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
